text:
ravi: hey, first-day blocker. trying to push to redwood/model-registry and keep getting 403. web says 'You must authorize SAML SSO' even though i'm in the org. accepted invite with ravi.personal@gmail.com then re-accepted with ravi@redwood.com.
it-support: welcome! can you paste the git remote and the exact error? also are you using HTTPS or SSH?
ravi: remote is https://github.com/redwood/model-registry.git. `git push origin main` -> `remote: Permission to redwood/model-registry.git denied to ravipersonal.` then it prompts for credentials. i created a PAT earlier for a third-party CI but maybe that's interfering.
mona: if you're pushing over HTTPS and have an old PAT or cached credentials in the OS keychain, git might be using the wrong account. run `git credential-osxkeychain erase` (mac) or check `git credential-manager` on Windows, or just `gh auth login --web` to refresh.
ravi: ran `gh auth status` -> shows logged in as ravi@redwood.com but CLI says SSO not authorized. also tried `gh auth login --with-token` with my PAT.
infra-bot: SCIM: user ravi@redwood.com provisioned at 2025-07-02T15:12Z -> teams: ml, models. SSO: pending authorization.
it-support: PATs need to be authorized for org SAML. If you generated a PAT before completing SSO, GitHub blocks it for org repos until you authorize the token. Go to Settings > Applications > Authorized GitHub Apps or check your org card in Profile -> Organizations -> click "Authorize".
ravi: clicked the org card and authorized SSO. still prompted for credentials when pushing.
mona: while you were doing that, i noticed something odd: your public key fingerprint matches a deploy key on redwood/docs-site (read-only). if the same key is a deploy key on another repo GH will ignore it for your account. run `ssh-keygen -lf ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub` to get the fingerprint and i'll check.
ravi: fingerprint `SHA256:ABCfakefingerprint12345`
mona: yep that fingerprint is listed as a deploy key on docs-site. deploy keys are attached to repos, not users, so even if it's your key GH treats it as repo-scoped. add a different key to your account or remove the deploy key. i've opened a ticket to move that key to your user account instead.
it-support: quick workaround: switch to SSH with a dedicated key for work and update remote: `git remote set-url origin git@github.com:redwood/model-registry.git`. make sure your SSH agent is offering the correct key (`ssh-add -l`).
ravi: created `~/.ssh/id_ed25519_redwood`, added the pub to my GitHub account, ran `ssh -T git@github.com` -> `Hi raviredwood! You've successfully authenticated...` changed remote to SSH and pushed — succeeded. :tada:
sam: note for onboarding doc: add steps to 1) prefer work email invites, 2) explicitly authorize SAML before creating PATs, 3) avoid reusing same SSH key as a deploy key. i'll file a doc patch.
infra-bot: ticket INF-3421 created to reassign deploy key and add onboarding checklist item.
it-support: great detective work everyone, welcome aboard @ravi :wave:
